VBO:0200039.summary: Merry and keen to work in its breed ideal, the American Cocker Spaniel is a flushing dog as well as a companion. The standard calls for an even temperament, with speed, endurance and smooth movement for the field. ASCOB names its solid colours other than black, from cream and buff through red and brown.
VBO:0200039.shortDescription: A merry, even-tempered flushing spaniel in the breed ideal; ASCOB covers its solid colours other than black.

VBO:0200624.summary: Close attachment to its people is central to the Great Dane's breed ideal, alongside confidence and a friendly manner. Some reserve with strangers is also described. Black and harlequin dogs share the breed's temperament standard; a Berlin committee united earlier large-dog types under the Great Dane name in 1878.
VBO:0200624.shortDescription: A devoted, friendly companion in the Great Dane's breed ideal, with confidence and some reserve around strangers.

sources.title: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Standard 235: Great Dane
sources.evidence: FCI235 Behavior/Temperament describes friendly, loving devotion to owners, possible stranger reserve and desired confidence. Historical Summary records a Berlin committee in1878 bringing earlier named types into Deutsche Doggen. Colour lists black and harlequin within variety2; these share the breed-level character standard. Ears explicitly naturally pendant, high-set, medium-sized with front edges close to cheeks. Tail reaches hocks, tapering naturally and hanging with a curve in repose. No child suitability, measured age/size, guaranteed behavior, color-specific temperament or aggression prediction used.

VBO:0201017.summary: Watchfulness and a friendly manner sit together in the Phu Quoc Ridgeback's breed ideal. Vietnam's standard describes an agile hunting dog able to change direction quickly, climb, jump and dig. Its history is tied to hunting alongside islanders on Phu Quoc, Vietnam, and a ridge of reverse-growing hair marks its back.
VBO:0201017.shortDescription: An alert, friendly hunting dog in Vietnam's breed ideal, with quick turns, climbing, jumping and digging in its repertoire.

VBO:0200133.summary: Beagliers tend to seek close company, following their people through the day and joining in games and walks. This Beagle–Cavalier King Charles Spaniel cross is described as playful and energetic, with a companionable side when the activity ends. The name covers first-generation crosses as well as reported Beaglier-to-Beaglier breeding.
VBO:0200133.shortDescription: A Beagle–Cavalier cross that tends to stay close to its people, joining in play and walks before settling nearby.

VBO:0200731.summary: Danny was a friendly school visitor who enjoyed making new friends and listening to stories. Introduced by Smith’s Wood Primary Academy in 2020 as nearly four years old, he visited each week. He was a Jackshund, a Jack Russell Terrier–Dachshund cross.
VBO:0200731.shortDescription: Danny, a Jack Russell–Dachshund cross, was a friendly weekly school visitor who enjoyed listening to stories.

VBO:0200904.summary: In Greece’s breed ideal, the contemporary Molossus of Epirus is devoted to its flock and owner and friendly with familiar people. Its work is guarding livestock in Epirus and nearby mountain areas, protecting flocks against large predators when needed.
VBO:0200904.shortDescription: A contemporary Greek livestock guardian, described as devoted to its flock and owner and friendly with familiar people.

VBO:0201086.summary: Flock protection is the Pshdar’s documented work in the mountain villages of Iraqi Kurdistan. Shepherds keep these dogs to guard against wild animals, and farmhouse guarding is another recorded use. Iraqi Pshdars have also been brought into Iranian Kurdistan for breeding and guarding.
VBO:0201086.shortDescription: A Kurdish working dog used to guard flocks and farmhouses, with Iraqi dogs also raised across the border in Iran.

VBO:0200180.summary: Described as energetic and eager to work in Texas’s state-dog resolution, the Blue Lacy has roots in cattle and hog herding. Its scent-trailing ability also serves hunting work. The Lacy family developed it in Burnet County, and the legislature named it the state dog breed in 2005.
VBO:0200180.shortDescription: A Texas ranch dog with cattle-herding and scent-trailing roots, named the state dog breed in 2005.
